AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Sex hormone binding globulin (SHBG) is the main transporter of sex hormones in most vertebrates. Low SHBG levels have been linked to increased propensity for diabetes and metabolic syndrome. Polymorphisms of the SHBG gene linked to low SHBG protein levels, also strongly predicted increased risk of type 2 diabetes, thus raising the possibility that SHBG may play a role in the in the pathogenesis of insulin resistance and diabetes.

AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: To examine whether expression of human SHBG in mice may ameliorate the development of diabetes and metabolic syndrome in response to a high fat diet.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Transgene mice expressing a human SHBG transgene (SHBG+) and their wild type littermates were fed high fat diet (HFD).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: HFD induced comparable obesity in control and SHBG+ mice. Male transgenes had higher muscle mass after 2-3.5 months HFD (0.43±0.028 vs. 0.38±0.053 gr, p=0.05). Fasting blood glucose, as well as insulin or HOMA-IR were not different in transgenic vs. wild type males. Female transgenes had higher fasting glucose (152.3±28.7 vs. 114.5 ± 27.2 mg/dl, p=0.01), but mean insulin and HOMA-IR were not different. Likewise, insulin tolerance test and intra-peritoneal glucose tolerance test (GTT) were not different. Only ovariectomized SHBG+ female mice (OVX), which gained weight similarly to controls and showed a lower increase in glucose during GTT. Finally, SHBG+ mice were not different from controls in terms of liver enzymes, serum triglyceride levels and blood pressure.
